name: Clay
tagline: The AI-powered GTM platform that made 'GTM engineering' a job title — now near US$7B
shortSummary: Clay is the New York AI platform for sales and marketing teams that created the 'GTM engineering' category, combining prospect data, AI research agents and automated growth workflows.

facts.label: Founders
facts.value: Kareem Amin (CEO); Nicolae Rusan; Varun Anand (COO, joined 2021)

facts.label: Sector
facts.value: AI-powered go-to-market (GTM) platform — data, AI agents, workflow automation

facts.label: Product
facts.value: Claygent AI agents, Sculptor workflow builder, 150+ premium data sources, CRM enrichment

rounds.label: Pre-Seed
rounds.note: Backing from NYC-based BoxGroup (David Tisch) at the company's founding.

rounds.label: Series A
rounds.note: Led by Sequoia (Alfred Lin) as Clay began building the GTM-engineering category.

rounds.label: Series B
rounds.note: Led by Meritech Capital as Clay entered its hypergrowth phase.

rounds.label: Series B Extension
rounds.note: Pre-emptive extension led by Meritech Capital, lifting the price to US$1.25B seven months after the US$500M Series B.

rounds.label: Employee Tender
rounds.note: Sequoia-led secondary tender allowing most employees to sell some shares.

rounds.label: Series C
rounds.note: Led by CapitalG (Alphabet's independent growth fund); Sapphire Ventures joined as a new investor. More than doubled the valuation from the January extension. Total funding reached US$204M.

rounds.label: Employee Tender
rounds.note: Employee tender led by DST Global at a US$5B valuation, nearly double the Series C mark seven months earlier.

rounds.label: New Round
rounds.note: Axios reported (31 August 2026) that Clay had inked a new round led by Wellington Management at a US$7B pre-money valuation. Round size undisclosed; as of 9 September 2026 neither Clay nor Wellington had formally confirmed the close — treat the figure as reported deal terms rather than a confirmed outcome.

sections.heading: Inventing the GTM-engineering Category
sections.body: Clay's founders (Amin and Rusan met at McGill studying electrical engineering, built and sold Frame, then took product roles at Dow Jones/WSJ) shipped Clay in February 2022 and effectively created two new categories: a 'claygency' services economy (160+ vetted partners) and the 'GTM Engineer' job title — 3,000+ open roles by January 2026 at a US$127K median salary. Customers like OpenAI, Anthropic, Canva, Intercom and Rippling use it to run outbound on the highest-quality data foundation.

sections.heading: Revenue Hypergrowth Without Touching the Bank
sections.body: Clay grew from US$500K ARR in 2022 to ~US$100M ARR by December 2025, with >200% NRR among enterprise accounts. After the August 2025 Series C, founder Amin told the press the company 'hasn't touched' the last round — the definitional capital-efficiency story of the AI GTM wave, and a reason Wellington's reported US$7B pre-money bet is on category ownership rather than current revenue.

sections.heading: A Valuation Arc With No Product Pivot
sections.body: Clay's ladder — US$500M (mid-2024) → US$1.25B → US$1.5B → US$3.1B (2025) → US$5B (Jan 2026) → a reported US$7B (Aug 2026) — rerated roughly 14x in two years without any strategic pivot, pricing AI-powered sales/marketing tooling as one of the defining software categories of the current AI cycle. Wellington's reported involvement mirrors its large late-stage checks into AI-native software (e.g. Glean) rather than waiting for IPOs.

sections.heading: The Caveat on the US$7B Round
sections.body: Unlike Harvey's September round, Clay's US$7B deal was still, as of 9 September 2026, an Axios-reported agreement in progress: round size and Wellington's stake undisclosed, and neither Clay nor Wellington had confirmed a close. Reported late-stage terms sometimes shift before finalizing, so the figure is carried here as reported rather than confirmed.
